replies.text: Japan’s demographic decline is definitely serious, but “extinction” may be too strong a word. The bigger question is how Japanese society will adapt while preserving its identity and culture.

comments.author: @dubski.0.1
comments.text: Interesting video. I follow several Japanese accounts on X and I noticed a rising discontent among many Japanese with the increase in migrant workers...particularly Muslims a lot of whom don't work but get lots of state handouts and benefits native Japanese who work hard and long hours don't get. The rise in traditional ancient Shinto temple fires too has been a real source of anger for many online. As a Scottish person living in the UK I've noticed a similar situation here too with Christian churches abandoned by the congregations being bought up and easily converted into mosques, or like in Japan and even some European countries where they're torched . A very sad situation with no easy solution.

replies.author: @TheCivilizedMind
replies.text: Thanks for sharing your perspective. Immigration, welfare, religion, and cultural change are highly sensitive issues, and online discussion can sometimes mix real concerns with claims that are hard to verify. It’s important to look at reliable evidence and avoid judging entire communities by the actions of a few.
